question: What year did Instagram launch?
explanation: Instagram launched on October 6, 2010, created by Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger and released exclusively for iOS. It reached 1 million users within two months and was acquired by Facebook (now Meta) in April 2012 for approximately $1 billion — a deal widely regarded as one of the most prescient acquisitions in tech history.

question: Which social media platform is known as 'the front page of the internet'?
explanation: Reddit is known as 'the front page of the internet' because its voting system surfaces the most popular content from across the web and its user communities, effectively curating what many people see as the most discussed and shared content online. Founded in 2005, Reddit consists of thousands of topic-based 'subreddit' communities.

question: What is the best-selling video game of all time?
explanation: Minecraft, developed by Mojang and released in 2011, is the best-selling video game of all time with over 238 million copies sold across all platforms as of 2023. Its open-world sandbox gameplay appeals to all ages, and Microsoft purchased Mojang for $2.5 billion in 2014. Tetris comes close when counting all versions combined, but Minecraft holds the single-title record.

question: What is the name of Kim Kardashian and Kanye West's first child?
explanation: Kim Kardashian and Kanye West named their first child North West, born in June 2013 — the name becoming a media sensation due to its double meaning as a compass direction combined with the surname West. Their subsequent children are named Saint, Chicago (Chi), and Psalm.

question: Which company owns Instagram and Facebook?
explanation: Meta Platforms, Inc. (formerly Facebook, Inc.) owns both Facebook and Instagram, as well as WhatsApp and Oculus/Meta VR. CEO Mark Zuckerberg rebranded the parent company from Facebook to Meta in October 2021 to reflect its broader vision beyond social media, particularly its focus on building a 'metaverse.' ByteDance owns TikTok, and Alphabet owns Google and YouTube.

question: What year did TikTok launch internationally?
explanation: TikTok launched internationally in 2018 after its parent company ByteDance merged it with the lip-sync app Musical.ly (which it had acquired in 2017), combining Musical.ly's existing Western user base with TikTok's features. The app had launched in China as Douyin in 2016 and in some international markets in 2017, but the major global rollout came in 2018.

question: Which singer held the record for most-streamed Spotify artist multiple years in a row before being surpassed?
explanation: Drake held the title of Spotify's most-streamed artist for multiple consecutive years, a feat driven by his prolific output and crossover appeal across hip-hop, R&B, and pop. Taylor Swift eventually surpassed him to become the most-streamed artist on Spotify, a remarkable achievement driven by her dedicated fanbase (Swifties) and catalog dominance.

question: What is the real name of rapper Cardi B?
explanation: Cardi B's real name is Belcalis Marlenis Almánzar, born in New York to a Caribbean family (her father is Dominican and her mother is Trinidadian). Robyn Fenty is Rihanna's real name, and Onika Tanya Maraj is Nicki Minaj's real name — both common distractors given their shared genre with Cardi B.

question: Which streaming service had the most subscribers as of 2023?
explanation: Netflix had approximately 260 million subscribers globally as of end of 2023, making it the world's largest subscription streaming service. Disney+ reached about 150 million subscribers, and while Amazon Prime Video has a large user base, its subscription count is bundled with Amazon Prime memberships, making direct comparisons complex — Netflix remains the clear leader by paid streaming subscriptions.

question: What does 'GOAT' stand for in sports and pop culture?
explanation: GOAT stands for 'Greatest Of All Time,' an acronym used to describe athletes, musicians, or other performers considered the best ever in their field. The term is widely used in sports debates (e.g., Michael Jordan vs. LeBron James in basketball), and rapper LL Cool J released an album titled 'G.O.A.T.' in 2000, helping popularize the usage.

question: Which artist holds the record for most Grammy wins?
explanation: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy Award wins in history, surpassing 32 wins as of 2024 — the most of any artist ever. She broke the record previously held by conductor Georg Solti (31 wins), and her wins span multiple categories including pop, R&B, rap, and music video.

question: What is the name of the fictional universe in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
explanation: The in-universe designation for the main Marvel Cinematic Universe continuity is Earth-616 in Marvel Comics lore, but the franchise itself is called the 'Marvel Cinematic Universe' (MCU). Within the MCU's multiverse storyline, the main timeline is sometimes referred to as Earth-616, though this differs from how that designation was originally used in comics.

question: What color is the Snapchat logo?
explanation: The Snapchat logo is yellow (specifically a bright, unmistakable yellow) featuring a white ghost icon against the yellow background. The app's signature yellow color is one of the most recognizable brand colors in social media, chosen to convey the app's youthful, fun, and spontaneous personality.

question: Which fashion brand is known for its interlocking 'CC' logo?
explanation: The interlocking double-C logo is the iconic monogram of Chanel, designed by founder Gabrielle 'Coco' Chanel. Gucci is known for its double-G monogram, Louis Vuitton for its LV monogram and damier pattern, and Versace for its Medusa head — each luxury brand's logo is distinct and trademarked.

question: What year did the first iPhone launch?
explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled and launched the first iPhone on January 9, 2007, at the Macworld Conference in San Francisco, describing it as 'an iPod, a phone, and an internet communicator' — 'three revolutionary products in one.' It went on sale on June 29, 2007, and fundamentally transformed the mobile phone industry and modern computing.

question: Which celebrity couple is known as 'Brangelina'?
explanation: The portmanteau 'Brangelina' refers to Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, who began their relationship while filming Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2004) and were together until separating in 2016 — their relationship and eventual split were among the most covered celebrity news stories of the 2000s and 2010s.

question: What is the name of Elon Musk's space company?
explanation: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.) was founded by Elon Musk in 2002 with the goal of reducing space transportation costs and eventually colonizing Mars. SpaceX became the first private company to successfully launch, orbit, and recover a spacecraft, and its Falcon 9 rocket has become the world's most launched orbital rocket. Blue Origin belongs to Jeff Bezos.

question: Which video-sharing platform was purchased by Google in 2006?
explanation: Google acquired YouTube in October 2006 for approximately $1.65 billion in stock, just 18 months after YouTube was founded by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen, and Jawed Karim. At the time, it was considered a staggering sum for a startup, but YouTube has grown into one of the world's most valuable media properties and the second most visited website globally.

question: What does 'NFT' stand for?
explanation: NFT stands for Non-Fungible Token, a type of digital asset recorded on a blockchain that certifies ownership and authenticity of a unique digital item. 'Non-fungible' means it cannot be replaced by an identical item (unlike a dollar bill, which is fungible because any dollar equals any other dollar); NFTs peaked in mainstream cultural attention around 2021–2022.

question: Which K-pop group's song 'Dynamite' was the first Korean song to debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100?
explanation: BTS made history in August 2020 when 'Dynamite' debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the first Korean-language group's song (and first fully English-language BTS song) to achieve that milestone. The achievement was driven by their massive global fanbase (ARMY) breaking streaming and sales records on release day.
